quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #21
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Roundabout ahead.
No passing zone.
Left turn yield on green.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a traffic signal is coming. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does a single broken white line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. You cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. You can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. You cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction. You can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction. You can pass when safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving the same way. Broken lines mean you can pass when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: U-turns are not allowed.
U-turns are allowed.
Winding road ahead.
Sharp left turn ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: U-turns are not allowed.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red slash means you cannot do that action. You cannot make a U-turn where this sign is posted.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Four-lane traffic ahead.
Divided highway ahead.
Two-way traffic ahead.
Intersection ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that you are entering a two-way traffic area.

questions.question: What does a solid white line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. You cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. You can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. You cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction. You can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction. You cannot pass.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving the same way. Solid lines mean you cannot pass.

questions.question: What type of sign is this?

options.text: Yield sign.
School crossing sign.
Stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield sign.
questions.explanation: A triangle pointing down is always a yield sign. Be ready to slow down or stop at a yield sign.

questions.question: What do pentagonal signs indicate?

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
Speed limits.
Railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zones.
questions.explanation: Five-sided signs mark school zones. Watch carefully for children and pedestrians when you see this sign.

questions.question: Which road is most likely to be slippery in cold weather after snow or rain?

options.text: A hilly, open road
A residential road
A road in a shaded area

questions.correctAnswerText: A road in a shaded area
questions.explanation: Shaded areas freeze before other roads and thaw later. Drive carefully on shaded roads when it is cold and wet.

questions.question: At what blood alcohol level can your license be suspended if you are under 21?

options.text: 0.15 percent or more.
0.08 percent or more.
Any amount.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any amount.
questions.explanation: Drivers under 21 cannot have any alcohol in their system. Any amount will result in serious penalties, including a two-year license suspension.

questions.question: If your car has Anti-Lock Brakes and loses traction on a slippery road, what should you do?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press and hold the brake pedal.
Press and hold the gas pedal.
Lightly tap the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Press hard on the brake pedal and hold it. Do not pump the brakes or let up on the pedal. The Anti-Lock Braking System will pump automatically. Steer away from danger while holding the brake.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a hill with a curb, which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.
Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.
Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
Keep your front wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb. This stops your car from rolling into traffic if your brakes fail. If there is no curb, turn the wheels toward the edge of the road.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT affect your blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: Your body weight.
How much you drink.
How much time passes between drinks.
How physically fit you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: How physically fit you are.
questions.explanation: Your BAC depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Physical fitness does not affect BAC. Neither does the type of drink or how well you think you can handle alcohol.

questions.question: Two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The largest vehicle has the right-of-way.
The car on the left has the right-of-way.
The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
The car on the right must yield to the car on the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
questions.explanation: When two cars arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The left driver can then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow arrow at a traffic signal?

options.text: Merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
Come to a complete stop.
Turn left after checking for oncoming cars and pedestrians.
You have the right-of-way and other traffic will stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn left after checking for oncoming cars and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow means you can turn left in that direction. But you must first yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, because they have a green light.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, what should you do with your front wheels?

options.text: Keep them straight and set the parking brake.
Turn them away from the curb.
Turn them toward the curb.
Turn the back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your front wheels away from the curb when parking uphill. If your brakes fail, your car will roll away from traffic instead of into it.

questions.question: When are streets and highways most slippery?

options.text: When it has been raining hard for several hours.
When they are clean and dry.
Just after it starts to rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just after it starts to rain.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery in the first half hour of rain. Water mixes with oil and dirt on the road, making it very slippery. Drive slowly and carefully during this time.

questions.question: When must you pull over for an emergency vehicle?

options.text: No matter which direction it is coming from.
Only if it is behind you.
Only if it is coming toward you.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter which direction it is coming from.
questions.explanation: You must pull over to the right edge and stop for any emergency vehicle with flashing lights. This is true whether it is coming from behind you or from the opposite direction.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with no warning lights or gates, what should you do?

options.text: Cross quickly as possible.
Always stop before crossing.
Be ready to yield to any train.
Speed up to beat any train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to any train.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to yield to any train before crossing. Do not cross until your entire vehicle can fit on the other side. Do not shift gears while crossing because your car could stall.

questions.question: How many feet away from a fire hydrant must you park?

options.text: 10 feet
15 feet
20 feet
25 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 10 feet
questions.explanation: It is against the law to park within 10 feet of a fire hydrant.

questions.question: How should you make room for cars entering the freeway?

options.text: Slow down.
Change to a different lane.
Keep your speed and position the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change to a different lane.
questions.explanation: If you can, move to another lane to create space for entering cars. If you cannot move lanes, slow down to help them merge safely into traffic.

questions.question: Leave more space than usual when stopping:

options.text: On a hill.
At an intersection.
At a stop sign.
At a toll plaza.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a hill.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space in front of your vehicle when stopped on an uphill slope. If the vehicle ahead rolls backward when traffic starts moving, you will have room to avoid a collision.

questions.question: At a school crossing sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop, even if there is no stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk your horn when you see children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Pentagon-shaped signs mean you are near a school zone or school crossing. When you see these signs, stay alert and be prepared to stop.

questions.question: When entering a freeway on a short ramp with no acceleration lane, you should:

options.text: Enter the far-right lane right away and speed up to match traffic.
Use the shoulder to get up to the speed of traffic.
Speed up and enter only after you find a gap in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up and enter only after you find a gap in traffic.
questions.explanation: When entering a freeway on a short ramp with no acceleration lane, wait for a gap in traffic before speeding up and entering. Stay stopped while waiting for a safe gap to appear.

questions.question: When a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line mark the road, with the broken line on your side, you may pass if:

options.text: It is an emergency.
You are on an expressway.
Traffic is clear.
It is at an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is clear.
questions.explanation: When the road has a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line with the broken line on your side, you may cross and pass if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Signs for public recreation areas are what color:

options.text: Orange.
Red.
Green.
Brown.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brown.
questions.explanation: Brown signs point to areas of cultural, historical, or public recreation interest. They help you find these places when traveling in unfamiliar areas.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who must you yield to?

options.text: Any driver who arrived before you.
The driver on your right, no matter who arrived first.
The driver on your left, no matter who arrived first.
The driver across from you, no matter who arrived first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any driver who arrived before you.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, the first driver to arrive goes first. If two or more drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, you should not:

options.text: Continue on the freeway and take an alternate route.
Drive to the next exit, leave the freeway, and return to your correct exit.
Back up on the road or shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back up on the road or shoulder.
questions.explanation: Never back up on a freeway or shoulder. Continue to the next exit. Other drivers do not expect vehicles to back up, and this will likely cause a crash.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should always:

options.text: Stop, listen, and go slowly.
Look to the left and right sides of your vehicle.
Slowly pass vehicles that seem to be stopped for no reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the left and right sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: At places where people may cross your path or where traffic lines meet, look left and right to make sure nothing is coming.

questions.question: When two vehicles enter an intersection at the same time from different roads, who must yield?

options.text: Either one
The vehicle on the left
The vehicle on the right
Neither

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left
questions.explanation: At intersections with or without signs or signals, when two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: Your accelerator sticks open while driving on a busy street. You should:

options.text: Blow your horn.
Slam on the brakes.
Turn on your four-way flashers.
Turn off the ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If the accelerator sticks, the engine will keep running. Turn off the ignition carefully by moving the switch only enough to stop the engine without locking the steering wheel. Then apply the brakes and move to a safe area.

questions.question: When stopping on snow or ice, what should drivers do with Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
Stay off the brakes and wait for the car to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
questions.explanation: With ABS, press the brake pedal firmly when stopping on snow or ice. The ABS will pump the brakes faster than you can.

questions.question: What is the best way to stay safe when backing your vehicle?

options.text: Honk your horn before shifting into reverse.
Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
Check your rearview mirrors to see what is behind you.
Turn up the car radio before backing up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
questions.explanation: Backing is difficult because drivers cannot see clearly behind their vehicles. Walk to the back of the vehicle before entering it to check for children and small objects.

questions.question: Before turning left, what is important to do?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Yield to oncoming vehicles.
Swing to the right side of your lane.
Wait until oncoming traffic has a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: When turning left at a traffic signal, you must yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, what should you do after setting the parking brake?

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires straight ahead.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking facing uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and turn your steering wheel away from the curb. If your vehicle rolls, it will roll into the curb.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians walking along the road ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
Pedestrians must not cross here.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers that pedestrians may be crossing. If a pedestrian is in a crosswalk, you must stop and stay stopped until they leave the crosswalk.

questions.question: When driving to an unfamiliar area, what should you do?

options.text: Depend on road signs to find your way.
Plan your trip in advance.
Only know generally where your destination is.
Always choose the most direct route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan your trip in advance.
questions.explanation: When driving to an unfamiliar area, plan your trip in advance. Check the location on a map before you start driving.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down or stop.
Stop if necessary.
You must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop at the marked stop line and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: The light is green but heavy traffic is coming. What should you do to turn left?

options.text: Use the next intersection.
Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Take the right-of-way since you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: When turning left with oncoming traffic, wait for the traffic to pass. You may enter the intersection to prepare for your turn if the light is green and no vehicle ahead of you is turning left.

questions.question: Stopping completely, yielding to cross traffic and pedestrians, then proceeding when safe matches which traffic light?

options.text: A solid red light.
A flashing yellow light.
A solid green light.
A flashing red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.

questions.question: What do broken yellow lines mean on streets and highways?

options.text: Indicate no passing zones.
Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.
Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Broken lines mean passing is allowed when safe.

questions.question: When you see a steady green arrow at a traffic signal, what should you do?

options.text: Merge into the lane pointing in the direction of the arrow.
Slow down and stop if it is safe.
Turn in the direction of the arrow. First, yield to any vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection.
Drive straight through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn in the direction of the arrow. First, yield to any vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you may turn in that direction. You must be in the correct lane for that turn. Always yield to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Stop, look for traffic, then go if the road is clear.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and drive carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: Why should you increase your distance behind a large vehicle?

options.text: So you can see around the sides of the vehicle.
Because other drivers will cut in front of large vehicles before passing.
Because following too close will pull your car into the vehicle's slipstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: So you can see around the sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Truck, bus, and van drivers cannot see you if you drive directly behind them. Keep more distance between you and large vehicles. This also helps you see the road ahead better.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You are about to enter a one-way street going the wrong direction.
U-turns are not allowed.
You may go if the path is clear.
You must come to a complete stop before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are about to enter a one-way street going the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: If you pass this sign, you are driving the wrong way and risk a head-on crash. Carefully turn around.

questions.question: What is a speed limit?

options.text: The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive under dangerous conditions.
The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive under good conditions.
The recommended speed to drive under good conditions.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive under good conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the highest or lowest legal speed you can drive under good conditions. You can drive slower than the posted speed, but you cannot drive faster. Drive slower in school zones, work zones, or when weather or road conditions are bad.

questions.question: You cannot drive faster than:

options.text: The posted speed limit.
A speed that is reasonable and safe.
A speed that is safe for current conditions.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must drive at a reasonable and safe speed. Consider the area, traffic, pedestrians, weather, road quality, and lighting. Always follow posted speed limits.

questions.question: When must you yield to other drivers?

options.text: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
When they are on your left at an unmarked intersection and you arrive at the same time.
When your traffic signal is a green arrow.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
questions.explanation: You must yield to other drivers when entering a street from an alley, driveway, or garage. You must also yield to pedestrians on a crossing sidewalk.

questions.question: You are driving on a road with two solid yellow lines dividing it. What can you do?

options.text: Cross these lines only to turn left into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.
Cross these lines to pass other vehicles if no traffic is coming.
Never cross these lines.
Cross these lines only to make a U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross these lines only to turn left into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction. You may only cross them to turn left into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.

questions.question: If dust or smoke blocks your view of other vehicles, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers.
Turn on your parking lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights whenever you cannot see other vehicles clearly. This also helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow in a traffic signal mean?

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It means the same thing as a red circular light.
Drivers may turn in the direction the arrow points.
Traffic in that direction must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a red circular light.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red circular light. Traffic in that direction must stop and cannot turn in the direction the arrow points.
